title: Google Cloud Adds Self-Managed VMware Cloud Foundation on Bare Metal
gist: Google Cloud made generally available a self-managed VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x offering on dedicated bare metal in 22 regions, joining Oracle and AWS in customer-operated VCF while keeping its managed VMware Engine. The launch, driven by Broadcom's VCF 9.x and license portability, omits pricing, SLA, region list and a migration path, and its TCO claims lack a baseline.

insights.claim: Google Cloud's new self-managed VMware option runs VCF 9.x on dedicated bare metal with root access across ESXi, vCenter and NSX in 22 regions, while its existing managed VMware Engine runs VCF 5.2 with Google handling lifecycle management.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Two-tier offering lets Google capture both control-seeking and hands-off VMware migrators.

insights.claim: The managed VMware model lets the cloud provider absorb Broadcom's release cadence and licensing changes, while the self-managed model hands both back to the customer in exchange for root access and running the current VCF major version.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Broadcom licensing churn is a real cost that shifts depending on who operates the stack.
insights.quote: The managed model lets the provider absorb Broadcom’s release cadence and licensing changes; the self-managed model hands both back
insights.locator: With this release, Google joins Oracle

insights.claim: Consultancy Xtravirt expects adoption of self-managed VCF to hinge on whether organizations actually want the operational responsibility, noting many want flexibility without doing 2am patching.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Adoption may be limited, pushing value toward managed-services partners.
insights.quote: Full control over your VCF estate is only worth having if someone in your organisation wants that responsibility.

insights.claim: Google's answer to the operational burden is its partner list, with Accenture, HCL, IBM, Infosys, TCS and Wipro among fifteen launch partners offering managed operations on top of the customer-owned stack.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Creates a managed-services revenue stream for IT services firms around VMware migrations.
insights.locator: Google's answer is the partner list

insights.claim: Google product leaders say Broadcom's launch of VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x is a key driver behind the self-managed deployment option.
insights.speaker: Sunny Dua and Prashanth Bungale
insights.so_what: Broadcom's product cycle is steering hyperscaler VMware strategy.
insights.quote: The launch of VMware Cloud Foundation 9.x by Broadcom is a key driver behind this self-managed deployment option.

insights.claim: Broadcom's VCF hyperscaler lead says license portability lets customers move existing VCF subscriptions to the cloud and run workloads unchanged.
insights.speaker: Abhay Kumar
insights.so_what: Portable subscriptions let Broadcom keep licensing revenue while workloads move to hyperscalers.

insights.claim: Google joins Oracle, which has offered customer-controlled vSphere since 2020, and AWS, which launched Elastic VMware Service in 2025 and added VCF 9.0 and 9.1 in July, while Azure VMware Solution remains Microsoft-operated.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Customer-operated VCF is becoming table stakes; Microsoft is the outlier.
insights.locator: With this release, Google joins Oracle

insights.claim: Google's self-managed VMware nodes are z3-highmem-192-highlssd-metal instances with 96 physical 4th-gen Intel Xeon cores, 1.5 TB memory, 72 TB local NVMe and 200 Gbps networking, with vSAN storage and NetApp Volumes as an external datastore option.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Large dedicated bare-metal hosts drive Intel server and NetApp attach demand inside Google Cloud.

insights.claim: Google's claims of up to 40% lower server TCO from NVMe memory tiering and up to 39% lower storage TCO from vSAN ESA are presented without baseline or methodology, and the only quoted customer, GXO Logistics, is at early assessment rather than production.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Treat TCO claims as marketing; early-stage customer evidence suggests slow ramp.
insights.locator: Storage is vSAN on the local NVMe

insights.claim: Google's self-managed VMware announcement provides no pricing, no SLA, no list of the 22 regions and no migration path from VMware Engine's VCF 5.2 to the self-managed 9.x stack.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Missing commercial details limit near-term revenue visibility and complicate upgrades for existing customers.

insights.claim: Before deployment, the customer project must enable VLAN-based networking, use an 8896-byte MTU VPC and pre-create management, vSAN, vMotion and two NSX subnets; after the installer, the environment is entirely the customer's.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Significant setup complexity favors partners and sophisticated VMware shops.
insights.locator: With the self-managed option, Google provisions
